title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 1 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Part 1 of NVIDIA's series introduces the Global Performance Tuner in TensorRT 11.1. The authors argue that hand-written default scheduling heuristics built from internal KPI models do not scale to diverse external models: they cause heuristic sprawl, entangle performance with accuracy and resist customization. They model the compiler as a builder algorithm that generates candidates and a search algorithm that picks the fastest one meeting the accuracy constraint, and they propose customizable build routes as the remedy.

insights.claim: TensorRT optimization has historically started from internal KPI models. Engineers encode patterns found in them as heuristics in the default scheduling strategy, and a heuristic that helps one model can cause regressions on unseen external models.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: NVIDIA acknowledges that one-size-fits-all inference compilation leaves performance unused on customer models, which is a reason for the shift to autotuning.
insights.quote: A heuristic inspired by one internal KPI model joins the shared strategy and may help familiar patterns while causing a regression for an unseen external model.

insights.claim: The authors identify three related problems with heuristic scheduling: heuristic sprawl makes code unmaintainable, performance-accuracy entanglement means reduced-precision kernels can exceed accuracy tolerance, and performance customization is hard across many models and GPUs.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: These pain points explain why inference stacks are adding search-based tuning, which raises build-time compute needs but lifts deployed throughput.

insights.claim: No single scheduling strategy is best for every model and deployment environment. A transformation that accelerates one network may slow another, and a kernel that is faster in isolation may interact poorly with fusion, layouts or memory traffic, effects that often appear only after the full engine is built and measured.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: End-to-end empirical tuning becomes necessary for inference cost optimization, which favours vendors with rich compiler toolchains.

themes.theme: Mathematical model of deep learning compilation

insights.claim: NVIDIA models a deep learning compiler as a tuple (A, B). Builder algorithm B maps a model to a set of solutions that satisfy an accuracy tolerance epsilon, and search algorithm A picks the minimum-runtime solution from that set.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Formalizing compilation as constrained search supports systematic automated tuning instead of hand-tuning.
insights.quote: A deep learning compiler can therefore be represented by an algorithm tuple (𝐴,𝐵), where 𝐵 generates candidate solutions and 𝐴 selects among them.

insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Gains will come from widening compiler option spaces over successive releases.

insights.claim: TensorRT's search can be suboptimal for two reasons. Heuristics may prune candidates, such as convolution tactics filtered by a channel-dimension threshold, before they are evaluated end to end. And kernels profiled in isolation behave differently inside the full graph, for example because of adaptive grid sizing on NVIDIA Blackwell GPUs.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Measuring local kernels misses end-to-end performance on new GPUs such as Blackwell, which argues for whole-engine benchmarking.
insights.quote: Consequently, the sum of individually measured kernel runtimes does not necessarily equal the end-to-end runtime.

insights.claim: Under a principle of determinism, a fixed program in a fixed environment has a fixed underlying runtime. If measurement noise is modeled as independent Gaussian noise, the average of repeated measurements is the maximum-likelihood estimate of the mean runtime.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: This is a methodological basis for reproducible benchmarking in automated tuning.

insights.claim: The Global Performance Tuner, released in TensorRT 11.1, rests on three principles: accuracy-aware tuning, customizable build routes, and a large solution space from which the fastest candidate within the numerical tolerance is selected.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: NVIDIA is deepening its software moat by automating per-model inference optimization on its GPUs.
insights.quote: Accuracy-aware tuning: Use end-to-end accuracy as a constraint that guides performance tuning.

insights.claim: Effective scheduling is model-dependent, so the optimal solutions for all models do not come from one universal build route. Different models can need different compiler component choices even on the same GPU.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Per-model tuning implies inference performance gains that default benchmarks may understate.
insights.quote: Consequently, the optimal solutions for all models do not necessarily originate from one universal build route.
insights.locator: Experience from performance analysis and optimization

insights.claim: The Global Performance Tuner validates each candidate solution against the specified accuracy criterion and measures end-to-end inference performance, then selects the minimum-runtime feasible solution from the union of solution sets produced by multiple build routes.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Tuning shifts compute cost from inference to build time, a favourable trade for high-volume deployments.
insights.quote: Among all solutions that meet accuracy requirements, the searching algorithm selects the minimum-runtime feasible solution from the expanded solution set.
